conviction_note: One asymmetric, one-sided item: ~$12M of IEEPA tariffs Duluth paid in FY2025 that it has applied to have refunded and explicitly excluded from both Q1 results and FY2026 guidance, in the exact quarter (ended 2026-08-02) in which comparable apparel importers booked their refunds in COGS; sized at ~65% odds it lands with this print, haircut for the risk it is stripped out of the adjusted figures and for a 20-day -13.4% drift I could not source.

findings.finding: On the 2026-06-08 Q1 call Duluth's CFO said 'For the IEEPA tariffs of approximately $12 million paid last year, we have applied for refunds but have not included any potential benefit in the results this quarter or in the full year guidance' - a windfall equal to ~8.7% of the $138M market cap and ~$0.32/share that is carried at zero in the affirmed FY2026 adjusted-EBITDA guide of $28-32M and in the single sell-side estimate of $(0.05), and Duluth's Q2 ended 2026-08-02, i.e. inside the window in which the rest of retail actually booked these refunds.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no option chain at all, one analyst estimate, and 46k shares a day of volume, so there is no preview note and no vehicle through which this could be expressed. More decisively, the tape did the opposite of pricing it: DLTH fell from a $4.27 August high to $3.62 and is -13.4% over 20 days, drifting down straight through the exact window (Target's $994M refund on 2026-08-20, Ross's $253M on 2026-08-27, CNBC's sector piece on 2026-08-30) when the tariff-refund windfall was the dominant retail-earnings story. If the market had connected a $138M-cap importer sitting on a $12M refund claim to that trade, the run-up would be positive and the stock would not be near the bottom of its August range. The disclosure exists only as one sentence of CFO prepared remarks on a June call; it is not in the Q1 press release headline items and it is in no aggregator's number - Duluth's own affirmed guidance and the lone $(0.05) estimate both carry it at zero, which is what 'not priced' looks like in the only two published figures that exist for this name.
findings.independence: Boot Barn - the closest listed workwear/DTC importer analogue - recognised $14.7 million of tariff refunds in cost of goods sold in a quarter that ended 2026-06-27, five weeks BEFORE Duluth's quarter end, per its 8-K exhibit dated 2026-07-29: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1610250/000110465926088137/boot-20260728xex99d1.htm . Separately Ross Stores' 10-Q for the three months ended 2026-08-01 - one day before Duluth's quarter end - recognised ~$253 million of the same IEEPA recoveries in cost of goods sold: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000745732/000074573226000041/rost-20260801.htm . And the mechanism timing is independent again: CBP's CAPE refund process opened 2026-04-20 with a stated 60-90 day turnaround once a declaration is accepted, per NRF on 2026-04-30 (https://nrf.com/blog/ieepa-tariff-refunds-are-moving-forward), which places a claim Duluth had already filed by 2026-06-08 squarely inside its own Q2. These are three different documents from three different filers, none of them the Duluth transcript.
findings.note_on_source_cluster: The Globe and Mail transcript at https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/DLTH-Q/pressreleases/2364690/duluth-dlth-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ carries the identical quote. It is the same underlying document (the 2026-06-08 call) and is cited only to verify the wording, not as a second data point.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any 8-K, press release or IR update between 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-02 confirming the refund had been received - the only company news since the Q1 print is a Minnesota Twins sponsorship (2026-08-10) and two product-marketing releases (2026-08-05, 2026-08-26), plus the 2026-08-20 earnings-date notice

Insider signal: the only Form 4s since the print are Garth Weber's 422-share tax withholding at $4.20 on 2026-07-25 and Scott Williams's 4,434-share director retainer award on 2026-08-02 - routine, no open-market buying or selling cluster (the widely circulated 'CFO buys DLTH' item is dated 2025-09-29 and is stale)

The two SCHEDULE 13G/A filings on 2026-08-07 turned out to be duplicate submissions by Askeladden Capital Management showing 1,698,483 Class B shares at 4.9%, with a date-of-event of 2024-08-09 - an administrative refiling of a two-year-old position, not a current change
A recent analyst catalyst: the Baird PT cut to $5 from $7 dates from the model update after Q3 2025, not from this quarter, so the 20-day -13.4% drift has no sell-side cause I could find

Demand-side scraping: Similarweb/Semrush gave no dated month-over-month traffic series for duluthtrading.com, and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment, so I could not date the change in the free-shipping threshold (currently $99+, with a 20%-off text offer as the deepest promotion on the homepage on 2026-09-02) against the $49-$50 threshold visible in older Slickdeals threads - the direction is consistent with the promotional reset holding but I have no sourceable 'before', so I have not filed it
Customer-revolt angle on the >50% cut in promotional days and 700bp reduction in discount depth: no datable forum, subreddit or review-volume evidence either way
Store closures / lease exits beyond the already-disclosed Salt Lake City fulfilment-centre closure in the Q1 10-Q; no new restructuring disclosure since
Going-private or control-transaction angle on the Class A/Class B structure: no 13D, no amendment, nothing
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up: the baseline's only directional input is a -13.4% 20-day drift and a -4.2% 5-day drift, and my finding is a positive, one-sided item worth ~9% of market cap that the drift has been moving away from rather than toward - with no option chain there is no skew to agree or disagree with, so the tape's downward drift is the entire priced view and this finding contradicts it.
